title: Graphs of Inverse Trigonometric Functions & Their Derivatives (AA HL)

questions.q: State the domain and range of $y=\arcsin x$.
State the domain and range of $y=\arccos x$.
State the domain and range of $y=\arctan x$.
Find the exact value of $\arcsin(\sqrt{3}/2)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arcsin(\sqrt{3}/2)=\pi/3$, since $\sin(\pi/3)=\sqrt{3}/2$ and $\pi/3$ lies in the range $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.

questions.q: Find the exact value of $\arccos(-1/2)$, in radians.
questions.answer: $\arccos(-1/2)=2\pi/3$, since $\cos(2\pi/3)=-1/2$ and $2\pi/3$ lies in the range $[0,\pi]$.

sections.heading: Differentiating arcsin using the chain rule
Differentiating arctan using the chain rule

questions.answer: By the product rule, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1\cdot\arccos(x)+x\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}\arccos(x)$. Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}\arccos(x)=-1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$, the second term is $-x/\sqrt{1-x^2}$. So $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\arccos(x)-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$.

sections.heading: Finding a gradient at a point

questions.q: Find the gradient of the curve $y=\arcsin(x/2)$ at $x=1$.
questions.answer: Simplifying first: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1/2}{\sqrt{1-x^2/4}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}$ (multiplying top and bottom by 2). At $x=1$, this is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, i.e. $\sqrt{3}/3$.

sections.heading: Deriving the derivative of arctan from first principles

questions.q: If $y=\arctan x$, then $x=\tan y$. Differentiate implicitly with respect to $x$ to show that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$.
questions.answer: Let $y'=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiating $x=\tan y$ implicitly with respect to $x$ gives $1=\sec^2y\cdot y'$. Since $\sec^2y=1+\tan^2y=1+x^2$ (using $\tan y=x$), this becomes $1=(1+x^2)y'$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$, as required.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the graph of $y=\arctan x$?
choices: An odd function with horizontal asymptotes $y=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
An even function with a vertical asymptote at $x=0$
A function with domain restricted to $[-1,1]$
questions.answer: $\arctan x$ is odd ($\arctan(-x)=-\arctan x$) and, as $x\to\pm\infty$, $\arctan x\to\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so its graph has horizontal (not vertical) asymptotes at $y=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and its domain is all real numbers, not $[-1,1]$.

sections.heading: Tangent line to an inverse trigonometric curve

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent line to $y=\arcsin x$ at $x=0$.
questions.answer: At $x=0$: $y=\arcsin(0)=0$. The derivative is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, which at $x=0$ gives gradient $1$. The tangent line is $y-0=1(x-0)$, i.e. $y=x$.
